title: Love★Com
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In Osaka, tall Risa Koizumi and short Atsushi Otani are classmates everyone treats as a comedy duo. They team up to win over their crushes, fail, and become close friends, until Risa realizes she has fallen for Otani. The shojo comedy follows her clumsy confessions and their relationship through the end of high school.
life_message: Love grows from honest friendship and courage, not from fitting what others expect of you.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Quarrels are slapstick and resolved by apology, not honor.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Risa defies the 'tall girl, short boy' expectation to choose freely.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friends, not family, carry most of the story.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Classmates are peers; little deference to rank.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern urban Osaka; no religious frame.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Being true to one's feelings is the core message.

folkways.japan: Osaka's comedic manzai culture and Kansai dialect shape the duo's banter, and confession culture (kokuhaku) structures the romance.

delivery.evidence: Carried by Risa and Otani's romance plot; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: The idea that couples need not match social expectations is carried by the central romance.

winners_losers: Risa and Otani win together; the expectation that couples must match by height loses. Sympathy goes to honest feelings.
